domain_reasoning: Most time is spent exercising the changed system, inspecting results, and recording evidence in test tools.
length_reasoning: A small change may need only a focused check, while a complex modification requires broader regression testing and defect documentation.
review_reasoning: The reviewer checks the coverage, evidence, and disposition, with more traces and defects to examine for a large cycle.
stakes_reasoning: A missed defect commonly causes user-facing rework, but a serious missed defect can cause an outage or data loss.
context_reasoning: Effective coverage depends on familiarity with the product, its test environment, and release conventions.

domain_reasoning: The evaluator spends most time researching candidates and trying their features in applications or trial environments.
length_reasoning: A comparison of a known candidate may take a few hours, while a multi-tool trial with integration and cost analysis can take several working days.
review_reasoning: The manager checks the criteria, evidence, costs, and recommendation, spending longer on evaluations with multiple trials and tradeoffs.
stakes_reasoning: A poor recommendation can lead to a reversible but costly tool choice, while a major adoption can create significant financial or security exposure.
context_reasoning: The evaluation needs familiarity with the team's workflows, existing tools, and procurement constraints.

domain_reasoning: The main work is modifying automated test code and running it against the changed product.
length_reasoning: A selector or assertion update can be quick, whereas a substantial product change may require rewriting and debugging several scripts; review and pipeline waiting are excluded.
review_reasoning: A reviewer inspects the code changes and test results, tracing more scenarios and dependencies for a larger update.
stakes_reasoning: A faulty script usually causes test rework or misses a defect, but inadequate coverage of a critical change can allow an outage or data loss.
context_reasoning: The worker needs familiarity with the product, test framework, and pipeline conventions.

domain_reasoning: Most investigation time is spent examining monitoring dashboards, logs, and performance traces.
length_reasoning: A known transient anomaly can be assessed quickly, while an intermittent or multi-component issue takes substantially longer to trace.
review_reasoning: The reviewer checks the finding against the alert and evidence, following more metrics and hypotheses for a complex investigation.
stakes_reasoning: A mistaken assessment generally causes further investigation, but a missed serious issue can contribute to an outage.
context_reasoning: Distinguishing expected behavior from a meaningful anomaly depends on detailed knowledge of the system and its performance history.

domain_reasoning: The main deliverable is a written procedure specifying prerequisites, steps, expected results, and required evidence.
length_reasoning: A short established procedure can be documented quickly, while a complex or compliance-sensitive procedure requires detailed checks and revisions.
review_reasoning: The reviewer reads the procedure against the standard and checks whether its steps and expected results are reproducible.
stakes_reasoning: An unclear procedure typically causes repeated testing or rework, but a compliance-sensitive omission can create regulatory exposure.
context_reasoning: The procedure must follow the organization's test conventions, repository practices, and applicable standards.

domain_reasoning: Building the environment chiefly involves installing software and changing infrastructure and application configuration.
length_reasoning: A reusable template can produce a simple environment in a few hours, while a complex production replica requires substantial configuration and verification; provisioning waits are excluded.
review_reasoning: Testers compare configuration and verification results with the production specification, checking more components and dependencies in a complex build.
stakes_reasoning: An inaccurate replica typically invalidates performance results, but configuration errors involving production connections or sensitive data can cause serious loss.
context_reasoning: Accurate replication requires detailed knowledge of the production architecture, dependencies, and environment constraints.

domain_reasoning: The representative checks account or order records and updates the case in service applications.
length_reasoning: A visible completed change can be verified in a few minutes, while discrepancies require tracing records and reopening the case.
review_reasoning: A supervisor checks the original remedy and system status, spending longer when records conflict or a case was reopened.
stakes_reasoning: A mistaken verification usually prolongs a reversible customer problem, but a missed billing or payment error can cause financial loss.
context_reasoning: The work requires familiarity with the company's account systems, case statuses, and resolution procedures.

domain_reasoning: Most active work is operating deployment, account, and configuration tools to prepare and verify the computer.
length_reasoning: A standard automated build needs limited hands-on work, while specialized software or configuration problems require more active setup and troubleshooting.
review_reasoning: A reviewer checks the ticket, login, required software, and security settings, with more checks for a customized workstation.
stakes_reasoning: A missing application usually delays the employee, but incorrect access or security configuration can expose sensitive data.
context_reasoning: The technician needs the employer's imaging, access, software, and security procedures.

domain_reasoning: Apart from talking, the representative mainly looks up product or service information in support and account systems.
length_reasoning: A straightforward answer takes a few minutes, while a question involving several products or eligibility details takes longer.
review_reasoning: A quality reviewer listens to the contact and checks the accuracy of the information against the relevant source.
stakes_reasoning: Incorrect information can reach the customer and cause a complaint or rework, but is usually correctable.
context_reasoning: The representative needs familiarity with the company's offerings, knowledge base, and service policies.

domain_reasoning: The representative enters the decided remedy in order, billing, or refund systems and records the action.
length_reasoning: A straightforward adjustment takes a few minutes, while an exchange or case requiring several account checks takes longer.
review_reasoning: The reviewer compares the approved remedy with the transaction and case note, checking additional records for a complicated case.
stakes_reasoning: An incorrect refund or adjustment can directly cause financial loss.
context_reasoning: The representative needs the organization's transaction systems, approval limits, and refund procedures.

domain_reasoning: The worker mainly configures a defect-tracking application, including fields, permissions, and workflows.
length_reasoning: A tracker based on an existing template can be set up quickly, while a customized workflow and permission model take several hours.
review_reasoning: The reviewer inspects the configured fields, access, and workflow and tries representative defect entries.
stakes_reasoning: Poor configuration typically causes team rework, but incorrect permissions can expose sensitive defect information.
context_reasoning: The setup must reflect the team's defect process, access rules, and existing tool conventions.

domain_reasoning: The representative verifies a written request and enters the relevant account transaction in company systems.
length_reasoning: A routine address change can be entered quickly, while a contract or discontinuance request may need additional checks and confirmation.
review_reasoning: The reviewer compares the request with the entered order and customer confirmation, checking more fields for a complex transaction.
stakes_reasoning: An incorrect order generally causes reversible service or billing rework, but an erroneous discontinuance or contract change can cause financial loss.
context_reasoning: Processing requires knowledge of the employer's account systems, verification rules, and order procedures.

domain_reasoning: The worker runs established diagnostic commands, observes outputs, and logs errors in support tools.
length_reasoning: A short routine check can be completed in minutes, while a round covering more systems or logging several errors takes longer.
review_reasoning: The reviewer checks the recorded results and tickets against the expected checks, spending more time when several errors were found.
stakes_reasoning: A missed routine error may require later rework, but a missed serious fault can contribute to an outage.
context_reasoning: The worker needs the site's checklists, system inventory, normal outputs, and ticketing conventions.

domain_reasoning: Most time is spent checking system status and logs, using administrative tools, and documenting the outcome.
length_reasoning: A known transient alert can be closed quickly, while a real slowdown may require a longer investigation and fix or escalation.
review_reasoning: The reviewer checks the alert, evidence, and disposition, following a longer diagnostic trail when a fix or escalation was needed.
stakes_reasoning: An incorrect assessment may cause additional support work, but a missed fault or bad fix can lead to an outage.
context_reasoning: Assessing the alert relies on detailed knowledge of the site's systems, normal performance, and prior incidents.

domain_reasoning: The main work is reading feedback, synthesizing findings into a report, and describing defects.
length_reasoning: A small test round can be summarized quickly, while a large round with varied feedback requires substantial consolidation and defect filing.
review_reasoning: The reviewer compares the report and filed defects with the collected feedback, checking more samples and priorities for a large round.
stakes_reasoning: An omitted or mischaracterized finding usually causes test rework, but a missed critical defect can contribute to a damaging release.
context_reasoning: The report depends on familiarity with the product, test objectives, defect categories, and stakeholder priorities.

domain_reasoning: Apart from talking, the representative mainly enters and verifies the transaction in order or billing systems.
length_reasoning: A simple agreed adjustment takes a few minutes, while an exchange or transaction requiring additional checks takes longer.
review_reasoning: A quality reviewer listens to the relevant contact and checks that the entered transaction matches the agreed remedy.
stakes_reasoning: An incorrect refund or billing adjustment can directly cause financial loss.
context_reasoning: The representative needs familiarity with the employer's transaction systems, policies, and approval limits.
